plants.summary: Fast-growing trailing vine that tolerates lower light and occasional missed waterings. Great for shelves and hanging pots.

light.notes: Bright indirect light keeps variegation strong. Low light is tolerated but growth slows and leaves turn greener. Avoid harsh afternoon sun, which scorches leaves.

water.checkBeforeWatering: Water when the top 2–3 cm of soil is dry. Slight leaf droop is a reliable 'I'm thirsty' signal.
water.method: Water slowly and evenly until it drains from the bottom, then empty the saucer after 10 minutes.
signsOfOverwatering: Yellow leaves, starting low on the vine
Black or mushy stems at the soil line
Soil stays wet for more than a week
signsOfUnderwatering: Soil pulling away from the pot edge

humidity.notes: Normal indoor humidity is fine. Misting adds little; group with other tropicals instead.

temperature.notes: Keep away from cold drafts and heater vents.

soil.mix: Standard houseplant potting mix with about 20% perlite or orchid bark.

fertilizer.notes: Fast leafy grower: nitrogen for leaves, potassium for strong stems.

homemade.name: Worm-casting tea (liquid feed)
homemade.how: Soak 1 cup of worm castings in 1 gallon (3.8 L) of water for 24 hours, stirring a few times, then strain. Dilute 1 part tea to 3 parts water. Use within 48 hours.
homemade.amount: Use it in place of the plant's normal watering amount shown in the app.
homemade.caution: Organic feeds can attract fungus gnats indoors. Let the topsoil dry between waterings.

homemade.name: Worm castings or home compost (top-dressing)
homemade.how: A gentle complete feed: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plus iron, manganese and zinc, released slowly. Scratch the soil surface lightly, sprinkle the castings around the stem (not against it), then water as usual.
homemade.amount: 1 tablespoon (15 ml) per 10 cm of pot width (e.g. 3 tbsp for a 30 cm pot). Keep the layer under 1 cm thick.
homemade.when: Once in March and once in July.

homemade.name: Dried banana-peel powder (potassium)
homemade.how: Fresh peels and banana water release very little and attract fungus gnats and fruit flies, so dry the peels instead: bake at 90 °C (200 °F) for 2–3 hours until brittle, grind to powder and keep it in a jar. It releases potassium slowly as it breaks down.
homemade.amount: 1 teaspoon (5 ml) per 15 cm of pot width, mixed into the top 2 cm of soil.
homemade.when: Once in March and once in June.
homemade.caution: A supplement, not a complete feed: mostly potassium. Use it alongside worm castings.

storeBought.name: Miracle-Gro All Purpose Plant Food 24-8-16
storeBought.how: The water-soluble powder you have. Stir until fully dissolved and use the mix in place of the normal watering amount. Water first if the soil is bone dry. It already contains iron, manganese and zinc. A mixed gallon keeps for a few weeks with the cap on.
storeBought.amount: ½ teaspoon (about 2.5 ml of powder) per 1 gallon (3.8 L) of water: the label's indoor rate.
storeBought.when: Every 4 weeks, March–October (skip the months you use worm-casting tea).
storeBought.caution: Use either this or a homemade liquid feed on a feeding day, not both.

signs: Roots circling or growing out of the drainage hole
repotting.notes: Go up only one pot size; too large a pot stays wet and invites root rot.

pruning.how: Cut just above a leaf node to make the plant bushier. Remove yellow or bare stretches of vine. Cuttings root easily in water.

propagation: Stem cuttings with at least one node, rooted in water or moist soil (2–4 weeks)
growthTips: Pin trailing vines back into the pot or root cuttings in the same pot for a fuller look.
Rotate the pot every couple of weeks for even growth.
A moss pole or trellis encourages larger leaves.

problems.symptom: Yellow leaves, mostly lower on the vine
likelyCauses: Natural ageing of old leaves (one at a time is normal)
problems.fix: Let the top 3 cm dry before watering again, empty the saucer, and remove yellow leaves.
Water more consistently and flush the soil with plain water every few months.

problems.symptom: Long bare stems with small, far-apart leaves
problems.fix: Move closer to a bright window (no direct afternoon sun) and prune leggy stems.

problems.symptom: Black or mushy stems at the soil line
problems.fix: Unpot, cut off brown/mushy roots, repot in fresh dry mix, and root healthy cuttings as backup.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.signs: White cottony clumps in leaf joints and under leaves; sticky residue.
pests.treatment: Dab with a cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol, then spray with insecticidal soap weekly for 3 weeks.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.signs: Fine webbing, tiny pale speckles on leaves, dull dusty look.
pests.treatment: Rinse leaves in the shower, isolate the plant, and apply insecticidal soap or neem oil every 5–7 days for 3 weeks.

pests.name: Scale
pests.signs: Small brown bumps on stems and leaf undersides that scrape off.
pests.treatment: Scrape off and wipe with alcohol; follow with neem oil weekly.

toxicity.notes: Chewing causes immediate mouth and throat irritation, drooling and swelling. Keep vines out of children's reach and wash hands after pruning. Call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) if swallowed.

companions.notes: Pairs well with other aroids that like the same moisture rhythm.

plants.summary: Upright succulent-like plant that thrives on neglect. Overwatering is the main way to kill it.

light.notes: Grows fastest in bright indirect light and handles a few hours of direct sun. Survives low light but grows very slowly.

water.checkBeforeWatering: Water only when the soil is completely dry all the way down. When in doubt, wait another week.
water.method: Water the soil, not the leaf rosette, until it drains. Never let it sit in water.
signsOfUnderwatering: Leaves feel thin and soft but not mushy

humidity.notes: Dry indoor air is ideal. Do not mist — water sitting in the rosette can cause rot.

temperature.notes: Cold, wet soil is the biggest risk; keep away from cold windows in winter.

soil.mix: Cactus/succulent mix, or potting mix with 40–50% perlite or pumice.
soil.drainage: Drainage hole essential; terracotta is a good choice.

fertilizer.type: Balanced liquid fertilizer or cactus fertilizer
fertilizer.notes: Very light feeder: one or two feeds a year is plenty. Over-feeding causes weak, floppy leaves.

homemade.name: Worm castings or home compost (top-dressing)
homemade.how: A gentle complete feed: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plus iron, manganese and zinc, released slowly. Scratch the soil surface lightly, sprinkle the castings around the stem (not against it), then water as usual.
homemade.amount: 1 tablespoon (15 ml) per 10 cm of pot width. Snake plants need very little.

storeBought.name: Miracle-Gro All Purpose Plant Food 24-8-16
storeBought.how: The water-soluble powder you have. Stir until fully dissolved and use the mix in place of the normal watering amount. Water first if the soil is bone dry. It already contains iron, manganese and zinc. A mixed gallon keeps for a few weeks with the cap on.
storeBought.amount: ¼ teaspoon (about 1.25 ml of powder) per 1 gallon (3.8 L) of water: half the label's indoor rate; snake plants need very little.
storeBought.when: Twice a year: April and July.
storeBought.caution: Use either this or a homemade liquid feed on a feeding day, not both.

signs: Roots cracking or bulging a plastic pot
repotting.notes: Likes being snug in its pot. Use a heavy pot for tall plants so they don't tip.

pruning.how: Remove damaged leaves by cutting at the soil line with a clean knife. Don't trim leaf tips — a cut leaf won't grow taller.

propagation: Division: separate pups with their own roots when repotting
Leaf cuttings in water or soil (slow; variegated yellow edges are usually lost)
growthTips: More light, not more water, is what speeds up growth.
Wipe dust off leaves monthly with a damp cloth.
Expect 2–4 new leaves a year indoors — that's normal.

problems.symptom: Soft, mushy or brown leaf bases
problems.fix: Unpot, cut away all soft tissue, let it dry for 2 days, repot in dry gritty mix and wait a week before watering.
Give a thorough soak. If the soil was wet, check the roots for rot instead.
Let the soil dry fully, move to brighter light, and support or remove floppy leaves.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.signs: White cottony spots where leaves meet the soil.
pests.treatment: Swab with 70% isopropyl alcohol, then insecticidal soap weekly for 3 weeks.

pests.name: Fungus gnats
pests.signs: Small black flies around the soil; larvae in damp topsoil.
pests.treatment: Let the soil dry out completely between waterings and use yellow sticky traps.

toxicity.notes: If chewed, can cause nausea, vomiting or mouth irritation. Low risk but keep out of reach of small children.

companions.notes: Group with succulents and ZZ plants that share its dry watering rhythm, not with humidity-loving tropicals.

plants.summary: Large climbing aroid famous for split, holey leaves. Needs bright light and something to climb to mature.

light.notes: Bright indirect light is needed for new leaves to split (fenestrate). A little morning sun is fine; harsh afternoon sun burns the leaves.

water.checkBeforeWatering: Water when the top 5 cm of soil is dry.
water.method: Water thoroughly until it drains, then empty the saucer.
signsOfOverwatering: Dark brown patches with yellow halos

humidity.notes: Prefers 50%+ but tolerates 40%. A humidifier or grouping with other tropicals helps more than misting.

soil.mix: Chunky aroid mix: potting soil, orchid bark and perlite in roughly equal parts.

fertilizer.notes: Big leafy grower: nitrogen for leaves, potassium for strong stems, magnesium for deep green.

signs: Roots out of the drainage hole
Aerial roots everywhere and soil dries in a day or two
repotting.notes: Add or extend a moss pole when repotting.

pruning.how: Cut damaged or yellow leaves at the stem base. To control size, cut stems just above a node; aerial roots can be tucked into the soil or trimmed.

propagation: Stem cuttings with a node and ideally an aerial root, rooted in water or sphagnum moss
growthTips: Give it a moss pole to climb; climbing plants produce bigger, more split leaves.
Wipe leaves monthly so they can use all available light.
Rotate every two weeks so it doesn't lean toward the window.

problems.symptom: New leaves have no splits or holes
problems.fix: Move to brighter indirect light and add a climbing pole. Splits appear as the plant matures.

problems.symptom: Yellow leaves, mostly lower on the plant
problems.fix: Let the top 5 cm dry out before watering; check that the pot drains.
Water more consistently and raise humidity by grouping plants or using a humidifier.

problems.symptom: Brown spots with a yellow halo
problems.fix: Cut off affected leaves, avoid wetting the leaves, and improve airflow. If spots keep spreading after two weeks, isolate the plant and discard badly affected leaves in the trash, not the compost.

pests.name: Thrips
pests.signs: Silvery streaks and tiny black specks on leaves; distorted new growth.
pests.treatment: Rinse the plant, then spray with insecticidal soap or spinosad weekly for 4 weeks. Isolate it from other plants.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.signs: Fine webbing under leaves, pale stippling.
pests.treatment: Shower the leaves, isolate, then neem oil or insecticidal soap every 5–7 days for 3 weeks.

pests.name: Scale
pests.signs: Brown bumps on stems and leaf veins.
pests.treatment: Scrape off, wipe with alcohol, then neem oil weekly.

toxicity.notes: Leaves and stems cause mouth and throat irritation and swelling if chewed; sap can irritate skin. Keep out of children's reach and wear gloves when pruning. Call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) if swallowed.

companions.notes: Grouping with pothos and other aroids raises local humidity for both.
